name: MathCanvas-Bench
intro: MathCanvas-Bench 是用于评测大型多模态模型内在视觉思维链能力的开放式数学基准。论文从约 63.2 万组初高中多模态题目与解答出发，经两轮 GPT-5 清洗、文本与图像去重、SwinIR 图像增强、GPT-4.1 类别标注及按类别占比 0.7 次方加权抽样构建测试集；论文概称 3K 题，固定公开版本实际包含 3,079 题。其余训练候选仅在训练分支执行五元词组 Jaccard 泄漏检查，公开 MathCanvas-Instruct 固定版本包含 218,604 题。官方评测器使用 GPT-4.1 提取并判断答案部分，仅将 API 与结构化解析成功且部分数为一至四的记录计为有效评测；完整准确率与加权准确率均以 valid_evaluations 为分母。
org: Multimedia Laboratory (MMLab), The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Huawei Research, BUAA
eval_feature: 答案级裁判, 图文交错输出
intro_en: MathCanvas-Bench is an open-ended mathematics benchmark for evaluating intrinsic visual chain-of-thought in large multimodal models. The paper starts from about 632K middle- and high-school multimodal problem–solution pairs, applies two GPT-5 filtering rounds, text and image deduplication, SwinIR image enhancement, GPT-4.1 category labeling, and category-proportion-to-the-0.7 weighted sampling. The paper rounds the test set to 3K, while the pinned public release contains exactly 3,079 problems. Only the remaining training candidates undergo the 5-gram Jaccard leakage check; the pinned MathCanvas-Instruct release contains 218,604 problems. The official evaluator uses GPT-4.1 to extract and judge answer parts, counts only API/schema-successful records with one to four parts as valid evaluations, and divides both Complete Accuracy and Weighted Scoring by valid_evaluations.

drawio_review_note: Primary-source review passed on 2026-07-21 against arXiv:2510.14958v1 Sections 3.1.2–3.2 and Appendix C, the official shiwk24/MathCanvas repository at commit 9b48cc81ab1f63d418a954e4502c3c6274068a7b (https://github.com/shiwk24/MathCanvas/tree/9b48cc81ab1f63d418a954e4502c3c6274068a7b), the MathCanvas-Bench Hugging Face revision 52ab630135728de9dbc1d1a724ebcf613678b8b3 (https://huggingface.co/datasets/shiwk24/MathCanvas-Bench/tree/52ab630135728de9dbc1d1a724ebcf613678b8b3), and the MathCanvas-Instruct revision fa759293ced51819bbfca63c09cb834b20ddb140 (https://huggingface.co/datasets/shiwk24/MathCanvas-Instruct/tree/fa759293ced51819bbfca63c09cb834b20ddb140). The benchmark JSONL is byte-identical between the pinned code and dataset snapshots, has SHA-256 7fdafe1d32109429d9c5e343e8aa5e1149eab4efe7bf13ec0e6f965c43eeda69, and contains exactly 3,079 records across eight categories; this reconciles the paper's rounded 3K wording. The pinned Instruct parquet manifest totals exactly 218,604 rows, reconciling the paper's approximate 219K. Construction preserves the 632K → 367K → 303K → 222K funnel, SwinIR and 512 × 512 normalization, GPT-4.1 taxonomy, benchmark-only MCQ exclusion, category-proportion-to-the-0.7 weighted sampling, and training-only removal when 5-gram Jaccard exceeds 0.4. The official evaluator at the pinned code commit concatenates only text reasoning steps, invokes gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 at temperature 0, parses multiple ground-truth parts only from explicit tags, inserts null for missing predicted parts, and records per-part booleans. One-part questions receive a binary score; two-to-four-part questions use normalized weights wi = 1.3^(i−1) / sum_j 1.3^(j−1), namely [0.4348, 0.5652], [0.2506, 0.3258, 0.4236], or [0.1616, 0.2101, 0.2732, 0.3551]. Complete Accuracy requires every part to be correct; Weighted Scoring averages per-problem weighted credit. The pinned summarizer skips API/schema failures after incrementing processing_errors and skips unsupported part counts after incrementing too_many_parts_skipped. It exposes stats['overall']['count'] as valid_evaluations and divides both complete_accuracy and weighted_accuracy by that value, not by all 3,079 release records. Direct inspection confirms the pinned benchmark contains only one-to-four-part ground-truth answers. Formal publication evidence [site-a11r-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2733×1141 (English) and 2733×1141 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2731×1139 and 2731×1139. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
